title: Fatality inquiry finds RCMP had little choice but to shoot Onoway man carrying knife
subtitle: A provincial court judge says two RCMP officers who fatally shot a man knife-wielding man who was threatening to kill someone took the "appropriate response." On Jan. 11, 2012, two RCMP officers from the Stony Plain detachment went to a domestic disturbance at the Onoway Apartments involving a man with a machete, says a fatality inquiry report released Monday.
article: A provincial court judge says two RCMP officers who fatally shot a man knife-wielding man who was threatening to kill someone took the "appropriate response."

On Jan. 11, 2012, two RCMP officers from the Stony Plain detachment went to a domestic disturbance at the Onoway Apartments involving a man with a machete, says a fatality inquiry report released Monday.
Earlier that day, Kayla Mahon told her father, Darby Mahon, that she and her estranged boyfriend had argued and he had pushed her.

Darby Mahon told his daughter he was going to kill her boyfriend, Elias Simon, because of what he'd done to her, the report says. That evening, Darby Mahon went to Simon's apartment, which was in the same building as his own. He was carrying a machete. Simon hid in a locked bedroom. Darby Mahon struck the door with the machete. Kayla Mahon tried to get the machete away from her father. When she did, Darby Mahon got a knife and started striking the bedroom door with it. Several tenants called 911.

While en route to the scene, Const. Kire Kondoski and Const. Daniel Lyon were told there was a baby in the apartment. They were told Darby Mahon had dropped his machete, but now had a knife. One victim had been cut and the Mahon was threatening other tenants to stay out of the way.

When the officers got to the building, they went to the apartment in the basement. They determined the situation was high risk and drew their weapons. They hollered "police" when they entered the apartment and saw an older man with a knife struggling with a woman.

They told him to drop the knife. Darby Mahon did not acknowledge the officers' verbal demands nor did he react to their presence, the report says. Darby Mahon turned toward Kondoski and approached him with the knife in hand. Kondoski could not back up any further, the report says, so when Darby Mahon was about two metres away, both Lyon and Kondoski fired their weapons. They struck him in the stomach and he fell. He was quickly treated by paramedics.

Mahon died from multiple gunshot wounds to his torso and lower extremities. A toxicology report showed he had alcohol, marijuana and prescription medications, Citalopram and oxycodone, in his system at the time.
Provincial court Judge Jacqueline Schaffter concluded that the use of lethal force in this case was reasonable in order for police to protect themselves and the other people in the apartment.
Fatality inquiries are held to determine if similar deaths can be prevented. The judge made no recommendations in this case.
